title: Referrals and repeat work from existing clients for Specialty appliance and machine cleaning
audience: Solo operators and team owners in a service business who want repeat bookings and referrals from clients they have already served.
learningOutcomes: Plan a review or referral request that is made after the client confirms the result and that the client can decline easily.
Write a next-service offer with a date, a scope and a price approach, and schedule the check-in that follows it.
Write referral reward terms, including the condition for payment, before any referral is made.

instruction.heading: Ask at the moment the client is most satisfied
instruction.body: The best time to ask for a review or referral is after the client has checked the appliance against the checklist and signed off, or when the invoice is paid. Ask in one sentence, name the next step you want, such as a review, and make it easy to decline. Record what you asked and what the client said. Timing matters: in one Baylor Keller Center experiment, a late reminder brought in more reviews than an immediate one (Baylor Keller Center, 2024). That is one experiment, so test the timing on your own clients. Google provides a review link or QR code for this purpose, and sending it is allowed. Do not write reviews for clients, do not screen out unhappy clients, and do not offer discounts or goods for reviews. The ACCC says incentives must be disclosed and must not depend on what the review says (ACCC, 15 July 2026).

instruction.heading: Offer the next service before the client leaves
instruction.body: At sign-off, propose the next visit with a date: the next clean of the same appliance, a clean of a second appliance in the home, or a membership tier if your own numbers show that it pays. Put the scope, the interval and the price approach in writing, and confirm the client agrees before you change their schedule. A membership tier is one vendor's repeat-client mechanism, not market evidence, so test it against your own costs first. The research found no sourced cleaning interval for appliances, so the interval is your own choice. If the written offer goes by email or text, check the electronic message rules first. ACMA's guidance indicates that inferred consent is narrow and does not cover a message sent just after a purchase (ACMA, read 4 November 2026).

instruction.heading: Check in at the interval that suits the service
instruction.body: Schedule a check-in after a period you can justify from your own records. A suggested starting point for a clean or repair is about ninety days, which is a choice to test, not a benchmark. The check asks whether the appliance still performs as the client expects, whether anything has changed and whether there is other work to quote. Keep it short, record the answer and reply to the client. A message that promotes a service can be commercial even when it is framed as a reminder, so check it under the Spam Act rules before sending. Remember that the cleaner does not repair an appliance's function, so direct any fault to the right licensed person.

instruction.heading: Re-contact previous clients before their busy periods
instruction.body: The research found no sourced seasonal pattern or maintenance interval for appliance cleaning, so plan any re-contact from your own booking records and test it. Offer the slots you can deliver, on written terms, with a clear way to opt out. Do not pressure anyone. Record each opt-out as soon as you receive it and stop sending to that client, because ACMA's guidance says an unsubscribe must be honoured within five working days (ACMA, read 4 November 2026). Gap: no verified landlord, property-manager or trade referral channel was found, so do not plan a referral stream on those assumptions.

instruction.heading: Set referral rewards in writing before anyone refers
instruction.body: A referral reward works best when the client knows the terms before they refer someone. Decide the reward, such as a credit on the next visit, and write down the payment condition, which is normally that the referred person has completed a paid visit. Tell the referrer the terms, and say what the reward is in the invitation. One study reported that stating the referrer reward in the invitation increased referrals (Xu, Yu and Tu, 2023). Get the referred person's consent before any referral message is sent, because the referrer's word alone may not be enough (Clayton Utz, 11 May 2017). Check any cash-based reward, and its tax or contract effect, with an adviser. No business.gov.au or ACCC guidance on referral rewards was found, so those points remain unconfirmed.

procedure: After each visit is signed off, make one review or referral request and record what was asked and the answer.
Write the next-visit offer with a date, scope, interval and price approach, and confirm it with the client.
Schedule the check-in for an interval you have tested, and send it using the electronic message rules.
Plan any re-contact message from your own booking records, and exclude anyone who has opted out.
Write the referral reward terms and the payment condition before the first referral is made.
When a referral books, confirm the referred visit is paid before applying the reward, and record the outcome.
Review at the end of each season which requests, offers and timings produced repeat work.

workedExamples.situation: A cleaner completes an oven and range hood clean for a client who rents a property. The client says she will recommend him to her landlord, who manages several flats. He wants to offer her a credit on her next visit if the landlord books.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should he do before the landlord books, and what should he avoid?
workedExamples.reasoning: He writes down the reward terms before any referral happens: the credit, the condition that the landlord's booking is paid, and when the credit is applied. He asks his client to pass on the landlord's details, and he contacts the landlord only if the landlord agrees. He does not promise a reward that is not written down. He does not publish photos of the flat, its address or the client's appliances without consent. He also checks that the referral does not turn into a promise about any appliance repair, because the cleaning does not include repairs or gas or electrical component work.

equipmentAndPpe: Client record with the sign-off date and the review or referral request made
Next-visit offer template with scope, interval and price approach
Calendar of re-contact dates based on tested timings
No PPE is needed for client follow-up; any site visit follows the site's own safety rules

commonErrors.error: Asking for a review before the client has checked the appliance and signed off.
commonErrors.prevention: Ask after sign-off or payment, when the client has confirmed the result is right.

commonErrors.error: Offering a referral reward that was never written down, so the terms are disputed later.
commonErrors.prevention: Write the reward and its payment condition before any referral is made, and give the referrer a copy.

commonErrors.error: Publishing a client's name, photo of a kitchen or property detail without consent for that use.
commonErrors.prevention: Get consent for each thing you plan to publish, and keep the record.

commonErrors.error: Contacting a client who asked not to hear from you, or using a re-contact message to pressure them. Gap: no verified client-channel evidence exists for appliance cleaning.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep an opt-out list, honour it at once, and keep re-contact messages factual and optional.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Publishing a client's name, photo, review or property detail needs the client's consent for that use. Do not write reviews on a client's behalf or invent them. OAIC guidance treats images in which a person's identity is clear, or can reasonably be worked out, as personal information, and says express consent is good practice (OAIC, last modified 26 February 2026).

The Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) may or may not apply to your business. The OAIC small business page sets a threshold of $3 million or less annual turnover, with some exceptions (published 10 March 2023). A law firm article reports that the small business exemption is still in force but under review (Warlows Legal, 20 July 2026). Confirm the current position before relying on it.

Review platforms and referral programmes can have their own rules on incentives. Google bans discounts or goods in exchange for reviews, and the ACCC says incentives must be disclosed and must not depend on the review's content. Check each platform's rules before offering any reward.

Check-in and re-contact messages sent by email or text can be commercial electronic messages under the Spam Act 2003 (Cth). A message that promotes any service can be commercial even when it is framed as a service reminder. Check each message before sending.

A referral does not extend the licence or insurance of the business that accepts the work. Gas and electrical component work needs the licence that applies in the state where the work is done. Victoria's rule is that only persons with a Type B gasfitting endorsement may work on Type B appliances (Energy Safe Victoria, reviewed 5 June 2024). This lesson does not grant any licence.

qualityStandard: Every review or referral request is made after sign-off or payment, and it includes an easy way to decline.
Every next-visit offer is written, has a date and is confirmed by the client before the schedule changes.
Every referral reward has written terms and a payment condition, and is paid only when that condition is met.
documentationEvidence: Review or referral request log with the date sent and the answer.
Next-visit offers with the date, scope, interval and client confirmation.
Referral reward terms with the referral record and payment outcome.
summary: Ask for reviews and referrals after the client has signed off, and make it easy to say no.
Offer the next visit in writing, with a date, before the client leaves.
Gap: no sourced cleaning interval, seasonal pattern, membership evidence or landlord or property-manager channel is verified for appliance cleaning.

knowledgeChecks.question: When is the best time to ask an appliance client for a review or referral?
options: Before the visit, so the client feels committed
After the client has checked the appliance and signed off
Only when the client has sent you a complaint

knowledgeChecks.question: A client wants to publish a review with her name and a photo of her kitchen. What do you need?
options: Her consent for the name and photo you plan to publish
Nothing, because the review is positive
Your own judgement that the photo looks professional

knowledgeChecks.question: What should a referral reward look like?
options: Paid to anyone who mentions your name
Decided after the referred person books, based on how keen the referrer seems
Decided and written in advance, with the condition for payment stated

knowledgeChecks.question: When does the lesson say to propose the next step for the client?

officialReferences.title: Avoid sending spam (ACMA)
officialReferences.covers: Says commercial messages need the recipient's consent, must identify the sender, and must include an opt-out that works for at least 30 days and is honoured within five working days. Does not mention one-to-one messages. Publisher: ACMA.

officialReferences.title: Online reviews for product and services (ACCC)
officialReferences.covers: Says incentives for reviews must be disclosed and must not depend on what the review says. Publisher: ACCC.
